chunks: 3. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abu Nasr, from al-Husayn ibn Musa, from 'Ubayd ibn Zurarah, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He (AS) said: I asked him about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'On the Day when there shall be a severe affliction.' He (AS) lifted the clothing that covered his shin, placed his other hand on his head, and said: 'Glory be to my Lord, the Most High!' The Compiler of this book says: The meaning of his statement 'Glory be to my Lord, the Most High' is that Allah, the Mighty and High, is far Exalted from having a shin.

key_terms.سَاق: Shin (a specific part of the leg, used here as a key term for divine attribute)
key_terms.يَوْمَ يُكَشَّفُ عَن سَاقٍ: On the Day when there shall be a severe affliction (literally: when the shin is uncovered)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic phrase 'Yawma yukshafu 'an saq' mean in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* addresses the debate between anthropomorphists (Mujassima) and rationalists regarding the phrase 'uncovering the shin' in Surah al-Qalam. It interprets the verse as a metaphor for divine readiness to execute judgment, supported by the Prophet’s glorification ('Subhan Rabbi al-A'la') which serves to negate physical limbs and attributes of limitation from Allah. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *tanzih* (transcendence) over *tashbih* (anthropomorphism).

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 3. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Isa on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abu Nasr on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Musa on the authority of `Ubayd ibn Zurarah that I enquired Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: “On the Day when there shall be a severe affliction.”

He (AS) lifted the clothing that covered his shin, placed his hand on his head, and said: “Glory be to my Lord, the Most High!” The Compiler of this book says; The meaning of his (AS) statement “Glory be to my Lord, the Most High” is that Allah, the Mighty and High, is far Exalted form having human attributes like a shin.
